missing_information_behavior: Do not recommend iron solely from vegetarian/vegan status. Use the dietary pattern as a prompt for assessment; without laboratory and current-use context, do not advance a supplement recommendation.
safety_exclusions: Diet pattern alone does not diagnose iron deficiency or anemia.
Do not recommend iron when known high intake, iron overload, or current iron treatment is reported.
Pregnancy, gastrointestinal disease, bleeding, anemia symptoms or abnormal laboratory results require clinician review.
professional_escalation_conditions: Known or suspected anemia or iron deficiency.
Pregnancy, heavy menstrual bleeding, gastrointestinal bleeding or malabsorption.
Hemochromatosis, iron overload, chronic disease or current iron therapy.
population_and_context: Vegetarian and vegan adults; non-heme iron bioavailability differs from heme iron, but individual status depends on intake, absorption, losses and physiology.
dose_constraints: No dose can be calculated from dietary pattern alone; use laboratory and professional assessment where deficiency is suspected.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS describes iron forms, bioavailability and higher reference requirements for vegetarian diets; it does not justify universal supplementation of vegetarians. This rule remains draft; source passage extraction, critical appraisal, certainty assessment and professional approval are required before activation.
